{{nihongo|'''Hananagakami Shrine'''|花長上神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mino Province]].

'''Hananagakami Shrine''' (はなながかみじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Ibigawa|Q1204046|qid=Q1204046}} (former {{ill|Tanigumi, Gifu|Q7683297|qid=Q7683297}}), {{ill|Ibi District, Gifu|Q1204309|qid=Q1204309}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|Q131277|qid=Q131277}}.

It is regarded as Hananaga Shrine of Ōno District, {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}}, in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, and its former {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine rank}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Summary ===
* Founding period is unknown. In the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, it was called Shichisha Myōjin.
* It has a close relationship with {{ill|Hananagashimo Shrine|Q11615718|qid=Q11615718}} in the same former Tanigumi Village. Akafusumainuōsumihikosawakeno-mikoto (deity of Hananagashimo Shrine) and Ame-no-Mikatsu-hime-no-Mikoto (deity of Hananagakami Shrine) are Izumo myth deities described in the '{{ill|Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|qid=Q11395858}}.' Hananagashimo Shrine is considered the male deity side and Hananagakami Shrine the female side (some say husband-wife deities). Also, the September 7 festival is held alternately by the two shrines. The distance between them is about 3 km.

=== Relationship with Azura Shrine ===
There is a close relationship with {{ill|Azura Shrine|Q11657682|qid=Q11657682}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|Q270810|qid=Q270810}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}} (the Engishiki-listed Azura Shrine of Niwa District, {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}). The enshrined deity is the same, Ame-no-Mikatsu-hime-no-Mikoto (Ame-no-Mikatsu-hime-no-Mikoto), and Azura Shrine preserves the following tradition:
* Prince {{ill|Homutsuwake no Mikoto|Q11631423|qid=Q11631423|lt=Honzuwake no Miko}}, son of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}}, could not speak even at age seven. In the empress's dream, Ame-no-Mikatsu-hime appeared and said: "No one has worshiped me until now. If you build a shrine and worship me, the prince will speak and fulfill his natural life." The emperor ordered Tatsuoka-kimi to find this deity.
* Tatsuoka-kimi climbed Hanakashika-yama in Mino (Hananagakami Shrine lies at its foot), made an azura garland from {{ill|Cleyera japonica|Q775470|qid=Q775470}} branches, prayed, and said: "Where this garland falls will be the place to worship the deity," then threw it far away. The place where it fell is said to be where Azura Shrine was founded.

=== Enshrined deities ===
There is also a theory that Hanakashika-yama itself is the sacred object.

*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Mikatsu-hime-no-Mikoto}}

=== Other ===
* Readings such as "Hanaka-kami-jinja" and "Hanakami-jinja" also exist. In 'Shikinaisha Chōsa Hōkoku' (Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai, Kōgakkan University Press), the reading is given as "Hananagakami-jinja." There is also a theory that "Hananaga" changed over time from an original reading "Hanaka."
* It was called Shichisha Myōjin because seven wooden images (including {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|Q3090037|qid=Q3090037}}, {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ar|أمه نو أوزومه|as|আমে-ন′-উজুমে|bcl|Ama-no-Uzume|ca|Ama-no-Uzume|cs|Ama no Uzume|de|Amenouzume|el|Άμε Νο Ουζούμε|eo|Ame no Uzume|es|Ame-no-Uzume|fa|آمه نو اوزومه|fr|Uzume|hr|Ame-no-Uzume|hu|Ame-no-Uzume|id|Ama-no-Uzume|it|Ama-no-Uzume|ja|アメノウズメ|jv|Ama-no-Uzume|ka|ამე-ნო უძუმე|ko|아메노우즈메|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯎꯓꯨꯃꯦ|no|Ama-no-Uzume|pl|Amenouzume|pt|Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto|ru|Амэ-но удзумэ|simple|Ame-no-Uzume|sv|Uzume|th|อาเมะ โนะ อูซูเมะ|tr|Ame-no-Uzume|uk|Ама-но-Удзуме-но-Мікото|zh|天鈿女命|qid=Q462803}}, {{ill|Dōsojin|Q269515|qid=Q269515}}, and {{ill|Yama-no-Kami|Q839254|qid=Q839254|lt=mountain deity}}) were once enshrined.
